title: My OSS Projects: AngleSharp
why_read: A personal retrospective from the creator of AngleSharp, a mature and widely used .NET HTML/CSS parsing library, explaining its design rationale and origin story.
analysis: AngleSharp is a well-established open-source .NET library providing a spec-conformant DOM implementation for parsing HTML, SVG, MathML, CSS, and XML without requiring a browser. This retrospective post explains why it exists, essentially as an alternative to fragile regex-based HTML scraping, and gives insight into long-term open-source maintenance. It's a solid, if narrow, technical read for .NET developers doing web scraping, testing, or headless DOM manipulation. The value here is mostly in maintainer perspective and design history rather than new technical content.
